name: Peter Singer
summary: Singer applies utilitarian ethics to public policy and personal conduct. He argues for equal consideration of comparable interests across species, greater assistance to people in extreme poverty, and legal access to voluntary assisted dying.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: In All Animals Are Equal, Singer identifies the ability to suffer or enjoy life as the basis for having interests and argues that comparable suffering should count equally across species.

humans-entitled-to-use-animals.rationale: In Equality for Animals?, Singer rejects a general human entitlement to exploit animals and argues that their interests cannot be discounted merely because they belong to another species.

abortion-legal.rationale: Singer explicitly defends a legal right to end an unwanted pregnancy safely, at least until very late pregnancy when fetal capacity for pain might be present. He describes this as his settled position since the 1960s.

assisted-dying.rationale: In Taking Life: Humans, Singer defends legal voluntary euthanasia under safeguards that include a competent, voluntary request and an independent medical opinion.

nation-first.rationale: In the opening chapter of One World, Singer argues that national governments must take responsibility for effects beyond their borders and criticizes the use of domestic economic interests to block climate cooperation.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: In Climate Change, Singer calls for rapid cuts in greenhouse gas emissions and assigns affluent, high-emitting countries a stringent duty to act.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: In Rich and Poor, Singer argues that affluent countries should greatly increase aid for people in absolute poverty and that a national border does not cancel the obligation to prevent severe deprivation.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Singer urges the left to judge proposals by whether they improve the lives of the poor and oppressed. In The Most Good You Can Do he applies the same emphasis on measurable effects to choices about how to help.

political-violence-legitimate.rationale: In Civil Disobedience, Violence and Terrorism, Singer rejects a blanket condemnation of political violence and argues that exceptional cases can be justified by their consequences. He condemns terrorism directed at the public in nearly absolute terms.

animal-use-humane.rationale: In Taking Life: Animals, Singer allows that raising some animals for food can be permissible if they lack self-awareness, live good lives and are killed painlessly. He doubts these conditions are often met in practice.

democracy-best.rationale: In Civil Disobedience, Violence and Terrorism, Singer argues that majority voting is the best available way for an egalitarian society to settle disputes peacefully, even though majorities sometimes choose badly.

property-fundamental.rationale: In Rich and Poor, Singer explicitly rejects a strong individualistic right to retain wealth, arguing that the unequal distribution of natural resources makes such entitlements depend too heavily on luck.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: In A New Standard for Giving, Singer proposes a graduated giving scale under which wealthier people give a larger proportion of their income to reduce severe poverty and prevent avoidable deaths.

military-force-for-human-rights.rationale: Singer endorses the international responsibility to protect people facing grave abuse by their own governments and discusses military intervention to stop the Rwandan genocide as a case for that responsibility.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Singer welcomes the International Criminal Court as a means of bringing genocide and crimes against humanity under international jurisdiction and criticizes the United States for withholding support.

free-trade.rationale: No recorded position found on whether all groups would eventually benefit from free trade.

religious-exemptions.rationale: In The Use and Abuse of Religious Freedom, Singer rejects a general exemption for conduct claimed to be religiously motivated and limits accommodation to cases where the law prevents people from practising their faith.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: In Free Speech, Muhammad, and the Holocaust, Singer defends the freedom to mock religious figures, reject belief in God and criticize religious teachings publicly.

criminalize-genocide-denial.rationale: In Free Speech, Muhammad, and the Holocaust, Singer calls for repeal of laws criminalizing Holocaust denial and argues that historical falsehoods should be challenged through evidence and argument.

holocaust-denial.rationale: In Free Speech, Muhammad, and the Holocaust, Singer describes David Irving's denial as false and endorses educating people about the historical evidence for the Nazi atrocities.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: In The Use and Abuse of Religious Freedom, Singer argues that secular lawmakers have no reason to adopt a religious community's valuation of Torah study when deciding whether to grant an exemption from military service. He applies independent ethical criteria to the laws discussed in the essay.

evolved-behavioural-sex-differences.rationale: Singer argues that evolved differences between the sexes may help explain differences in willingness to subordinate other interests to career advancement.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: In Paris and the Fate of the Earth, Singer calls on affluent countries to decarbonize and to refuse licences for new coal mines.

gm-crops.rationale: In A Clear Case for Golden Rice, Singer endorses growing genetically modified crops that can address serious nutritional needs or resist drought, with regulation tailored to their benefits and risks.

human-caused-global-warming.rationale: In Climate Change, Singer accepts the evidence attributing current warming to human greenhouse gas emissions and argues that high-emitting countries must cut those emissions.

opposition-only-legal-channels.rationale: In Civil Disobedience, Violence and Terrorism, Singer defends unlawful opposition to extreme injustices in dictatorships and says that protest outside legal channels may also be justified in democracies.

direct-action.rationale: In Civil Disobedience, Violence and Terrorism, Singer defends elected decision-making and assigns civil disobedience a role in publicizing issues or prompting reconsideration when normal channels fail.

property-sabotage-justified.rationale: In Civil Disobedience, Violence and Terrorism, Singer argues that serious harms can sometimes justify damage to property. He weighs the harm to owners and others against the benefit expected from the action.

means-match-ends.rationale: No recorded position found on whether methods of social change should reflect the desired social order.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: In Civil Disobedience, Violence and Terrorism, Singer argues that a wrongful majority decision can still create a moral reason to comply, though sufficiently grave injustice can outweigh it.

state-harmful.rationale: In Civil Disobedience, Violence and Terrorism, Singer argues that settled laws, authoritative judges and enforcement are needed to keep the peace given how people actually behave.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Singer describes progressive taxation as the fairer way to finance collective poverty relief because those with the greatest means would bear a greater share of the burden.

harm-principle.rationale: Singer discusses paternalism as a policy option and argues that whether a restriction for adults' own good is justified depends on its consequences, including the risk of government abuse.

one-party-rule.rationale: In Civil Disobedience, Violence and Terrorism, Singer argues that contested questions should normally be decided by genuine majority voting and rejects abandoning majority rule for government by a chosen few.

strong-leader.rationale: No recorded position found on whether a strong leader should bypass gridlock.

limit-population.rationale: In Rich and Poor, Singer supports voluntary measures such as access to contraception and education to address high population growth alongside poverty reduction.

initiating-nondefensive-force-unjustifie.rationale: Singer argues that military intervention to protect people from grave abuses by their own government can be justified. He treats the failure to intervene in Rwanda as a case in which international action was called for.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Singer argues that progressive financing of global poverty relief would be fairer because people with the largest incomes can contribute substantially more of their income than people with little to spare.

traditional-family.rationale: Singer and Sagan argue that a stable family can provide a loving home for children across several family arrangements, including blended families and couples who do not marry. They reject treating the decline of heterosexual marriage as evidence of social decline.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Singer and Sagan include married same-sex parents among the family arrangements that should be accepted in the absence of evidence of harm to children or adults.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: In Equality and Its Implications, Singer defends using affirmative action to address the exclusion of disadvantaged minorities from institutions and professions, with the choice of policy depending on evidence that it works.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: In One Law, Singer proposes replacing permanent-member vetoes with a supermajority on a reconstituted Security Council and argues that a reformed council could impose sanctions on states that currently hold vetoes.

universal-morality.rationale: Singer says that moral judgments can be objectively justified by reasons accessible to any reasoning being. He describes this as a change from his early noncognitivism.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: In Should We Honor Racists?, Singer criticizes Woodrow Wilson for reinstating racial segregation in federal offices and describes it as one of the racist policies for which Wilson should be held responsible in public remembrance.

population-transfer.rationale: In One Law, Singer endorses international protection against ethnic cleansing and rejects a claim to sovereignty that would allow governments to carry out or permit such abuses.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: In A Better World? Singer advocates strengthening supranational institutions in stages, giving them authority over specific issues such as transnational environmental and labor standards.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: In One Economy, Singer argues that the WTO or a body with authority over global trade should set and enforce basic standards covering worker safety and union rights.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: In Equality and Its Implications, Singer argues that appropriately applied racial preferences can promote equality and should be judged on their effectiveness.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: In An Assessment, Singer rejects Marx's prediction of inevitable collapse from capitalism's internal contradictions as a failed forecast. He argues in a later Green Agenda interview that alternatives to global capitalism have become less plausible.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Singer argues that accumulating possessions and pursuing an ever-higher material standard of living can be collectively self-defeating and that using surplus income to reduce suffering offers a more worthwhile goal.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: In Civil Disobedience, Violence and Terrorism, Singer grounds reasons to obey laws in effects such as maintaining peaceful decision-making and avoiding enforcement costs. When those reasons do not apply, he allows that a breach can be ethically unproblematic.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: In Homosexuality Is Not Immoral, Singer rejects criminal penalties for consensual same-sex acts and points to the blackmail, harassment and obstacles to HIV education created by India's sodomy law.

military-force-beyond-defence.rationale: In One Law, Singer defends the international responsibility to protect civilians from mass atrocities by their own government, including UN-authorized military intervention when necessary.

future-generations.rationale: Singer reaffirms the green ethic of preserving the environment over the long term and argues that the foreseeable harm to future generations is a reason to act urgently on climate change.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: In One Economy, Singer argues for using trade rules to benefit developing countries, including measures that give the least-developed countries a fairer share of trade growth. He also calls for ending rich-country farm subsidies that harm poorer producers.

shared-human-nature.rationale: In Equality and Its Implications, Singer rejects basing equal moral standing on a natural characteristic shared by all humans, including the capacity for a sense of justice, and grounds equality in the consideration of interests.

simple-living.rationale: In A New Standard for Giving, Singer urges people with enough to live comfortably to forgo discretionary luxuries and use part of their income to prevent suffering in extreme poverty.

wages-fall-to-bare-minimum.rationale: In An Assessment, Singer identifies near-subsistence wages as one of Marx's failed predictions and contrasts it with the rise in living standards of workers in industrial countries.

pay-for-effort.rationale: In Equality and Its Implications, Singer defends paying for need and effort instead of inherited ability and argues for narrowing pay gaps between senior management and people whose earnings barely meet their needs.

notes: Reviewed all active and candidate statements. Searched local books, public essays and interviews for political economy, constitutional and electoral rules, civil liberties, equality, culture and religion, war and intervention, global institutions, migration, aid, ecology, technology, and political methods. Follow-up research used the revised One World, Practical Ethics, Marx: A Very Short Introduction, and the Green Agenda interview to check sovereignty, racial preference, minority autonomy, alliances, and class and markets. Singer and Renata Singer also petitioned the Australian Parliament to restore voting rights for Australians living abroad. The quiz's local voting statement concerns foreign residents and asks a different question. Checked Project Gutenberg, Australian Hansard, MediaSum and the Lex Fridman interview index, distinguishing the philosopher from the military technology writer of the same name.
